people.name: Dr. Beau G. Schelble
people.bio: Dr. Schelble is an interdisciplinary researcher whose work sits at the intersection of human factors, human-centered computing, and AI. For nearly a decade he has explored how humans and AI can work together more effectively and safely — investigating trust, shared mental models, situational awareness, ethical AI behavior, and intelligent information sharing. His research spans defense, advanced manufacturing, healthcare, cybersecurity, and emergency response. He received his PhD in Human-Centered Computing from Clemson University in 2023 under advisor Nathan McNeese, and his BS in Psychology from Clemson in 2018.
people.shortBio: Assistant Professor of ISE. PhD in Human-Centered Computing, Clemson University 2023.

people.name: Sarah Mendoza
people.education: BS Psychology (Minor in Computer Science), Clemson University, 2025
people.bio: Hello hello! I'm Sarah Mendoza and I'm from Clemson, South Carolina. Guided by my curiosity for people and interpersonal behaviors, I graduated from Clemson University with my bachelor's degree in Psychology in May 2025. I was brought into the world of human-AI teams during my time there — researching everything from trust perceptions, to autonomy levels, to teamwork versus taskwork. This, coupled with my minor in Computer Science, has prompted me to further explore the various dimensions of human-AI teams within the ARCS lab! When I'm not working, I'm probably in the gym, checking out a new café, or playing The Sims 3.
people.shortBio: Research focus: trust perceptions, autonomy levels, and teamwork dimensions in human-AI teams.

people.name: Yayun Tian
people.education: MS Analytics, USC, 2022 · BS Applied Math & Statistics + Economics, Stony Brook, 2020
people.bio: Hi, I'm Yayun Tian, and I'm a Ph.D. student in Industrial and Systems Engineering at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville. I graduated from Stony Brook University in 2020 with a Bachelor's degree in Applied Mathematics and Statistics, a double major in Economics, and a minor in Computer Science. In 2022, I earned my Master's degree in Analytics from the University of Southern California, and then spent three years working as a software engineer in Los Angeles. These experiences led me to think about how technology could play a more active and supportive role in teamwork — not just as a tool, but as a trusted and capable teammate.
people.shortBio: Background in applied mathematics, statistics, and software engineering. Exploring AI as trusted teammate.

people.name: Naveena Nagaraju
people.education: MS Information Science, University of Pittsburgh, 2025
people.bio: Hi, I'm Naveena Nagaraju, and I'm a Ph.D. student in Industrial and Systems Engineering at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville. I graduated from the University of Pittsburgh in 2025 with a Master's degree in Information Science. During my master's, I worked with research labs at Pitt focused on AI, and after graduating I worked as a Data Analyst, which grew my interest in AI and how humans interact with it in everyday life even further. This interest goes back to my undergrad, and I'm excited to bring that experience into the ARCS lab and contribute to research on human-AI teaming.
people.shortBio: Background in information science and data analytics. Exploring how humans interact with AI in everyday life.
